  "title": "We don't know where our users are",
  "body": "Blocking https://github.com/bbc/psammead/issues/1957 being used in simorgh\r\n\r\n**Describe the bug**\r\nWhen simorgh was news articles only, we determined where a user was from a `BBC-ORIGIN` header sent from mozart. We use `headers['bbc-origin']` such that if it ends in `.co.uk` theyre in the UK, so show them the non-adverts cookie banner, else, show them the adverts cookie banner.\r\n\r\nSince simorgh has expanded out to the WS sites we lost use of this logic, as you can only hit them on `.com`, so you can only ever see the advert cookie banner.\r\n\r\nLuckily, this is the safest state to be in, as were showing messaging to people who dont need it, vs not showing it to people who do.\r\n\r\n**To Reproduce**\r\nSteps to reproduce the behavior:\r\n\r\nIn & Out of the UK\r\n1. Go to https://www.bbc.com/igbo\r\n2. See international cookie banner messaging\r\n\r\n**Expected behavior**\r\nIt shows the UK messaging if the user is inside the UK, even on `.com`\r\n\r\n**Possible fix implementation:**\r\nInstead of, or as well as the `bbc-origin` header, get an `isUK` header from mozart. This then needs to be baked into the page inside simorgh data, so on the client we know if theyre in or out of the UK (in place of fig). This info can then be used to show the right banner messaging and in future, adverts/not\r\n\r\n\r\n**Testing notes**\r\n\r\n- [x] This bug fix is expected to need manual testing.\r\n\r\n**Additional context**\r\nAdd any other context about the problem here.\r\n",

{
  "format": "coda-github-issue-snapshot",
  "format_version": 1,
  "artifact_id": "privacy-issue-linked-joomla-projects-privacy-framework-213",
  "issue_url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213",
  "source_issue_url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213",
  "api_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213",
  "title": "Missing consent \"evidence\" on contact form",
  "body": "Currently, when an user submits a request through the Contact Form he/she's prompted to grant a consent to process the request thanks to the new plugin, so the user has to flag the checkbox to proceed. And that's ok, but site owner must be able to demonstrate that the user gave his/her consent to process the request/data. \r\n\r\n### Describe the solution you'd like\r\nWe could have two opportunities:\r\n\r\n1. Add a copy of the consent statement in the email that is sent through the Contact Form.\r\n2. Record the consent in the Consent view within Privacy Dashboard (index.php?option=com_privacy&view=consents) \r\n\r\n",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2018-07-16T07:50:42Z",
  "updated_at": "2018-08-08T01:51:03Z",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": null,
  "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T07:21:27.187037+00:00",
  "comments_fetched_at": [
    "2026-11-05T07:21:27.187037+00:00"
  ],
  "expected_comment_count": 26,
  "retrieved_comment_count": 26,
  "comments_complete": false,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 405175249,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405175249",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T08:11:39Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T08:11:39Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "the fact that it is a required field is the evidence that the person consented.\r\n\r\nrecording the consent in the privacy dashboard is pointless as this contact form can be submitted by guest users"
    },
    {
      "id": 405182688,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405182688",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T08:47:36Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T08:47:36Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> recording the consent in the privacy dashboard is pointless as this contact form can be submitted by guest users\r\n\r\nThat is true.\r\n\r\n> the fact that it is a required field is the evidence that the person consented.\r\n\r\nThat would not so easy to bring as argument. It would be much better to have the statement in the email that is sent after form submission. "
    },
    {
      "id": 405186246,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405186246",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T09:02:32Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T09:02:32Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "do you require and record a consent before someone sends you an email?"
    },
    {
      "id": 405187421,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405187421",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T09:07:39Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T09:07:39Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Nope. But, if someone sends me a message through the website, i need to demonstrate that the user read and accepted the privacy policy shown on the website."
    },
    {
      "id": 405202243,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405202243",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T10:10:25Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T10:10:25Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "And com_contact doesn't store information in the DB, so I don't think it's needed to keep track of their consent in the DB (and then in that case you are finally storing their data)"
    },
    {
      "id": 405204084,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405204084",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T10:19:09Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T10:19:08Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> And com_contact doesn't store information in the DB, so I don't think it's needed to keep track of their consent in the DB (and then in that case you are finally storing their data)\r\n\r\nThat's why having a \"confirmation text\" in the email would be the perfect way to achieve it."
    },
    {
      "id": 405223940,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405223940",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T11:57:58Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T11:57:57Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "There is no hook system to alter emails, so without hardcoding things into com_contact, we can't change any email contents."
    },
    {
      "id": 405224389,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405224389",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T12:00:06Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T12:00:06Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> There is no hook system to alter emails, so without hardcoding things into com_contact, we can't change any email contents.\r\n\r\nIn this case i believe that hardcoding something like the following sentence is not so bad:\r\n\r\n `The user accepted the privacy policy to process this request on DATE`"
    },
    {
      "id": 405226720,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405226720",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T12:08:14Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T12:08:14Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "Not really.  It would only be true if the plugin asking consent is enabled and all the pre-conditions involving that has been set.  Even then, that means hardcoding a plugin's configuration into a component, which is not proper system design (a component should not be aware of a specific plugin's presence at all)."
    },
    {
      "id": 405227935,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405227935",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T12:13:51Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T12:13:51Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "You can't hard code it into the email because not all sites will require the consent"
    },
    {
      "id": 405557100,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405557100",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T11:59:38Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T11:59:38Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "I would see the situation in the following way: The spirit of GDPR is to make it obvious to the user what data a website collects about a person. In the case of a contact form, all data is provided by the user. So the consent of the user is given the moment that he typed it into the form. It is also not required that the user typed in real data. Long story short: For now I would say that the implicit consent was given when the contact form was filled out and the explicit consent was given when the checkbox was checked. That explicit consent is implicitly stored by the timestamp of the send mail.\r\n\r\nSo I would vote against coding anything into this and close this issue.\r\n\r\nOne thing that would also speak against storing this in Joomla would be, that sites without any interactive elements except for this contact form (like my own website for example) would then have to set up the whole privacy component. Right now a person could request all the data that I have about it and I would only have to go through the stuff on my local system. When you are storing this data in Joomla, you would have to provide that export, too.\r\n\r\nSo, nothing to do here, at least for now. We could revisit this issue when there are the first few decisions by courts."
    },
    {
      "id": 405579471,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405579471",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T13:21:45Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T13:21:45Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Personally, i don't think we should store the consent in the Privacy dashboard.\r\nPursuant the Italian Law, before GDPR, there was a similar \"consent\" mechanism that each website should have implemented and generally it has been done through a checkbox at the end of the contact form (obviously people used third-party extensions to achieve this).\r\nThe checkbox was something similar to \"I agree with the Privacy Policy of this website\" and this sentence was copied also in the email sent to the administrator.\r\nSomething like this has been mandatory in Italy (at least) from several years. \r\nAccording to GDPR, consents must always be explicit, clear, with clear purpose and so on... so even if i agree with you that if i contact you, i'm implicitly consenting you to process the data i submit, it would be good, if we can add to the email the consent sentence."
    },
    {
      "id": 405583564,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405583564",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T13:34:13Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T13:34:13Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "> it would be good, if we can add to the email the consent sentence.\r\n\r\nIt would be nice.  Our system capabilities do not allow us to do so without hardcoding com_contact to be dependent on the single privacy consent plugin that we ship in core.  We do not have a hook to alter emails when they are being sent in core, and arbitrarily adding the string to the email would be factually incorrect if you do not have any form of consent in place when submitting it."
    },
    {
      "id": 405586341,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405586341",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T13:42:52Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T13:42:52Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> Our system capabilities do not allow us to do so without hardcoding com_contact to be dependent on the single privacy consent plugin that we ship in core.\r\n\r\nI fully understand this. And what about extending com_contact instead of using the plugin?"
    },
    {
      "id": 405587962,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405587962",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T13:47:44Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T13:47:44Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "The only other option is to remove the consent plugin and put options in every component to do the same thing that the consent plugin is doing.  Then, because the options are within the component, could you alter the email body string conditionally without breaking any system rules."
    },
    {
      "id": 405595557,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405595557",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T14:10:21Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T14:10:21Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> The only other option is to remove the consent plugin and put options in every component to do the same thing that the consent plugin is doing.\r\n\r\nFor the contact form, i believe that would be appropriate and would satisfy the requirement."
    },
    {
      "id": 405598622,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405598622",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T14:19:25Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T14:19:25Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "1. this is not a gdpr solution\r\n2. This is just to help you along the way\r\n3. We can never address every countries unique interpretation of a law\r\n4. What were italian web sites doing before "
    },
    {
      "id": 405599569,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405599569",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T14:21:53Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T14:21:53Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "Making any changes for this specific if/else condition IMO opens too many cans of worms to reliably manage, because the scope of work I see it creating ends up in creating a lite version of com_content in com_privacy to have a single spot in core to define and manage the privacy policy (because you can't reasonably force com_contact to only support a com_content created privacy policy article)."
    },
    {
      "id": 405615057,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405615057",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T15:03:45Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T15:03:45Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> What were italian web sites doing before\r\n\r\nUsing different contact forms components.\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 405645312,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405645312",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T16:31:16Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T16:31:16Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "You are giving explicit consent to this when checking the checkbox. You are logging if the plugin is active in our actionlog. So you can say \"The user had to check the checkbox, otherwise the mail wouldn't have been sent and the checkbox was built in and working, because we have the enabling/disabling of the plugin logged in our log.\""
    },
    {
      "id": 405875874,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405875874",
      "created_at": "2018-07-18T09:49:35Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-18T09:49:35Z",
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "@jeckodevelopment\r\nYou can solve the problem by using the custom fields in this way ...\r\n\r\n1 - Create a new group of \"mail\" type fields and name it \"Privacy policy\".\r\n\r\n2 - Create a new additional field of type \"mail\" as follows:\r\n\r\nTitle > I declare that I have read and accepted the following Privacy policy\r\n\r\nType > Checkboxes\r\n\r\nRequired > Yes\r\n\r\nText > By sending us a message through this form, or by directly using the e-mail address indicated here, the processing of your personal data will be carried out in compliance with the EU Regulation 2016/679. The personal data you have provided may be processed in compliance with the aforementioned legislation. The Data Controller, in compliance with the Regulations, will take care of archiving for purposes consistent with the interactions shown by the Visitor and only for the time strictly necessary for the verification and evaluation of the information provided, for the purpose of exchanging information or contacts. To find out more about our privacy policies, please see the extended information at https://www.XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/privacy. To request information, changes, or to oppose the treatment and request the cancellation of your data, present in our archives, you can write to us via the address XXXXXXXXXX@XXXXXXX.XX.\r\n\r\nValue > The same policy entered in Text\r\n\r\nField Group > Assign the previously created group \"Privacy policy\".\r\n\r\nGo to the Permissions tab and set this...\r\nEdit Custom Field Value > Allowed\r\n\r\nIn this way, the privacy policy will be visible on the contact page, but will also be contained in the email."
    },
    {
      "id": 405877618,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405877618",
      "created_at": "2018-07-18T09:55:53Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-18T09:55:52Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "thanks @linuxpac , but i wasn't really looking for a solution for that :)\r\nMy suggestion was to implement the opportunity to add the statement into com_contact. \r\nAnyway, if you guys think that it's not necessary, feel free to close the issue.\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 405884419,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405884419",
      "created_at": "2018-07-18T10:21:45Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-18T10:21:45Z",
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "Ok, jeckodevelopment. However, this solution works well and also allows you to demonstrate that the visitor has read and accepted the policy (if you have activated the function \"Send Copy to Submitter\", even the sender will receive the email containing the declaration of acceptance of the policy with the policy itself)."
    },
    {
      "id": 409890580,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-409890580",
      "created_at": "2018-08-02T11:07:50Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-02T11:07:50Z",
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "It's easy to add such a phrase to the email body of the contact form with a small 3rd plugin. I didn't think too much about it but something like this should work:\r\n```\r\n public function onSubmitContact(&$contact, &$data)\r\n {\r\n  if (JPluginHelper::isEnabled('content', 'confirmconsent'))\r\n  {\r\n   if (isset($data['consentbox']) && !empty($data['consentbox']))\r\n   {\r\n    $data['contact_message'] .= \"\\n\\n\" . 'The user accepted the privacy policy to process this request on DATE';\r\n   }\r\n   // Nearly impossible(?):\r\n   else\r\n   {\r\n    // Say this \r\n   }\r\n  }\r\n  else\r\n  {\r\n   // Say that\r\n  }\r\n  return true;\r\n }\r\n```"
    },
    {
      "id": 411257564,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-411257564",
      "created_at": "2018-08-08T01:51:03Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-08T01:51:03Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "Closing this out.  Given the core architectural changes needed to properly support this it is too far out of scope to include here, and as pointed out it is possible to add this statement via plugin if so desired."
    },
    {
      "id": 411301558,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-411301558",
      "created_at": "2018-08-08T06:34:48Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-08T06:34:48Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Thanks"
    }
  ],

{
  "format": "coda-github-issue-snapshot",
  "format_version": 1,
  "artifact_id": "privacy-issue-linked-CityOfLosAngeles-mobility-data-specification-60",
  "issue_url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60",
  "source_issue_url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60",
  "api_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60",
  "title": "How should access to the 'provider' API be authenticated?",
  "body": "Given that the provider API is intended for use by cities (and their vendors/patners) and NOT the general public, how should providers implement access control on their API endpoints? \r\n\r\nSimple option would be for LADOT to issue a shared secret at the time when providers are granted an API.\r\n\r\nLonger term, probably need a more cryptographic or account-oriented solution, since cities may want the ability to authorize 3rd parties (e.g. vendors) to access MDS data on their behalf.",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2018-09-12T17:52:45Z",
  "updated_at": "2018-09-26T03:52:13Z",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": null,
  "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T07:23:23.662782+00:00",
  "comments_fetched_at": [
    "2026-11-05T07:23:23.662782+00:00"
  ],
  "expected_comment_count": 10,
  "retrieved_comment_count": 10,
  "comments_complete": false,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 420781126,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-420781126",
      "created_at": "2018-09-12T20:11:48Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-12T20:11:48Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "I’d argue that it might be a good choice to remove transport protocol completely from this spec, or at least put it into a separate optional spec. \r\n\r\nFor example, you could imagine a provider and agency agreeing that the provider just emails a large data dump of all trips every week or that the provider FTPs the data to a central server. Authentication would be figured out differently in each of those situations. "
    },
    {
      "id": 420786519,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-420786519",
      "created_at": "2018-09-12T20:29:49Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-12T20:29:49Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "@aickin that's an interesting thought, I can see how that kind of setup could be more useful to certain organizations that maybe aren't quite prepared to deal with API calls and AWS databases etc. \r\n\r\nThat being said... do we have any of those agencies listening in, that want to put forth their thoughts on this matter? Given that this is still early days for MDS, I would hesitate to add too many \"options\" for how to move this data around etc. until we've at least established the baseline spec and its utility. Unless we have a willing partner agency that wants to try a different transport protocol approach?"
    },
    {
      "id": 420786554,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-420786554",
      "created_at": "2018-09-12T20:29:56Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-12T20:29:56Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "I proposed a static file option in #58. Given the technical capabilities of LA and a few other cities, and the likelihood of vendors emerging to help cities consume real-time APIs, it seems wise to have a game plan on this. But for many cities, something far less sophisticated is likely the best option."
    },
    {
      "id": 420787745,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-420787745",
      "created_at": "2018-09-12T20:33:44Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-12T20:33:44Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "@thekaveman Good question. My guess is that the cities least equipped to deal with a full API are also the least likely to be hanging out in a GitHub issues list. Might need to figure out a way to do some outreach to them."
    },
    {
      "id": 420788016,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-420788016",
      "created_at": "2018-09-12T20:34:41Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-12T20:34:41Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "@LADOTBikeshare has been maintain a list of all the cities we've reach out to with email address, and there is also NACTO. "
    },
    {
      "id": 420806608,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-420806608",
      "created_at": "2018-09-12T21:37:55Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-12T21:37:55Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "I would suggest a [JWT](https://jwt.io/) that is issued by the provider to LADOT (or other agencies). This provides a lot of customization from the provider's perspective if there is other information they want to encode in the token and allows the providers to authorize accounts with well-defined permissions for accessing only MDS resources.\r\n\r\nFrom the agency's perspective it is also relatively easy to issue new tokens and track token usage to prevent improper access or sharing. We also have envisioned agencies being able to generate their own tokens with bounded from this master token for use by their employees or vendors which seems like a win.\r\n\r\nIf it's helpful would be happy to provide some example tokens and requests."
    },
    {
      "id": 422103343,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-422103343",
      "created_at": "2018-09-17T17:32:29Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-17T17:32:29Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@hunterowens yes. would be happy to."
    },
    {
      "id": 424829229,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-424829229",
      "created_at": "2018-09-26T18:51:13Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-26T18:51:12Z",
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "@jfh01 I completely agree that cities least equipped to deal with APIs are also least likely to see this thread. In terms of outreach, I've been talking to a number of cities and reviewing a number of policies throughout the US and think it would be a good idea for the folks working on MDS to reach out to some of the shared mobility program managers, especially in smaller-to-mid-sized cities. You can see which cities explicitly ask for APIs in column U here - https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ehA-PFoCnUswfOB7RaaguRN8xW5_khNvVWzOobsO_AA/edit#gid=0\r\n\r\nVery few of the cities I've talked to are equipped currently to deal with a full API. \r\n\r\nFull disclosure: I work for a company (Stae.co) that wants to help equip them to deal with a full API."
    },
    {
      "id": 425215189,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-425215189",
      "created_at": "2018-09-27T19:30:18Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-09-27T19:30:18Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "@SLarrick Great research notes!"
    },
    {
      "id": 425996507,
      "url": "https://github.com/CityOfLosAngeles/mobility-data-specification/issues/60#issuecomment-425996507",
      "created_at": "2018-10-01T17:38:58Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-10-01T17:38:58Z",
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "Yes, thank you @SLarrick! We’re doing a bit of research on API requests from cities. We are finding broad alignment on desire for an API without a lot of detail. We are discussing an officially-sanctioned MDS flat file converter tool at #58 which may help bridge the gap between keeping MDS sophisticated, simple, and accessible."
    }
  ],

{
  "format": "coda-github-issue-snapshot",
  "format_version": 1,
  "artifact_id": "privacy-issue-linked-dotnet-cli-3093",
  "issue_url": "https://github.com/dotnet/cli/issues/3093",
  "source_issue_url": "https://github.com/dotnet/cli/issues/3093",
  "api_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/dotnet/cli/issues/3093",
  "title": ".NET core should not SPY on users by default",
  "body": "@blackdwarf @piotrMSFT I am very disappointed to discover that .NET core comes with a hidden and enabled spy utility that reports on its users. (Lakshanf/issue2066/telemetry #2145). Apparently, MS has learned nothing from the backclash against Windows 10 spying on users. I suspect many will not want to install .NET core for this reason, which is a shame because .NET core is otherwise cool. \n",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2016-05-18T06:01:43Z",
  "updated_at": "2017-07-27T05:34:19Z",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": null,
  "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T07:21:29.283304+00:00",
  "comments_fetched_at": [
    "2026-11-05T07:21:29.283304+00:00"
  ],
  "expected_comment_count": 216,
  "retrieved_comment_count": 216,
  "comments_complete": false,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 220082687,
      "url": "https://github.com/dotnet/cli/issues/3093#issuecomment-220082687",
      "created_at": "2016-05-18T16:29:01Z",
      "updated_at": "2016-05-18T16:29:01Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "Our recent blog post discusses the addition of telemetry to the .NET Core tools. See: https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/dotnet/2016/05/16/announcing-net-core-rc2/#telemetry\r\n\r\nMe and the folks on my team are motivated to provide a great product. As you can also see from the blog post, we've made some pretty dramatic changes in RC2. We believe that they are the right ones, but we need both feedback and usage data in order to help us find all of the rough edges. Usage data tends to be more objective in the aggregate and user feedback more insightful, so we do a better job when we have both available.\r\n\r\nThe data we collect does not identify individual users. We're only interested in aggregate data that we can use to identify trends. The telemetry feature is configurable, so you can turn it on/off at any time. It is also scoped, only applying to tools usage, not the rest of the product. We think that this is a good trade-off and recognize that not everyone will like it. We do know, however, that many people will like the product improvements that will come from this insight.\r\n\r\nWe intend to share the data. The presence of it will do a lot to define the scope of data. It will also give the community access to the same insight we have. We very much feel that improving .NET Core is a shared need and task. As an example, we would welcome a PR from the community that added another telemetry data point given a strong improvement reason and no loss in anonymity.\r\n\r\nWe are separately considering *opt-in* runtime telemetry to learn more about crashes, GC pauses and startup time. There is no way we can get enough insight about the product without that kind of information. We are very focussed on constant improvement and will *transparently* do what it takes to ensure the product is compelling and competitive.\r\n\r\nAs an aside, it's been a busy week with shipping RC2 and answering questions. I haven't actually looked at this data yet and I'm one of the primary consumers. I'll be doing that today or tomorrow. I'm looking forward to sharing my insights."
    },
    {
      "id": 220094918,
      "url": "https://github.com/dotnet/cli/issues/3093#issuecomment-220094918",
      "created_at": "2016-05-18T17:10:59Z",
      "updated_at": "2016-05-18T17:10:58Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "@richlander\r\n\r\n> we need both feedback and usage data\r\n\r\nDoes the telemetry still include arguments provided to the `dotnet` command? In server hosting scenarios, some may have sensitive arguments passed to the command (for portable apps) that they wouldn't want leaked to MS.\r\n\r\n> and will transparently do what it takes\r\n\r\nThe program is not \"transparent\" IMO."
    },
    {
      "id": 220105007,
      "url": "https://github.com/dotnet/cli/issues/3093#issuecomment-220105007",
      "created_at": "2016-05-18T17:47:45Z",
      "updated_at": "2016-05-18T17:47:45Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "> Does the telemetry still include arguments provided to the  `dotnet`  command?\r\n\r\nMy understanding is that this was recently discussed with our privacy team and we concluded that collecting the arguments themselves (hashed or not) is not acceptable per our privacy policies. Not sure whether the code already reflects that, but it's being worked on."
    },
    {
      "id": 220106220,
      "url": "https://github.com/dotnet/cli/issues/3093#issuecomment-220106220",
      "created_at": "2016-05-18T17:51:56Z",
      "updated_at": "2016-05-18T17:51:56Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "> The program is not \"transparent\" IMO.\r\n\r\nWhat would you accept as sufficiently transparently? Not trying to say that we already are sufficiently transparent; I'm trying to understand your concern and what we could do make it better. The product is worked on by various team who all contribute to the same open source code base on GitHub. Clearly you think that's not sufficient, so I'd like to understand what would address that."
    },
    {
      "id": 220113052,
      "url": "https://github.com/dotnet/cli/issues/3093#issuecomment-220113052",
      "created_at": "2016-05-18T18:16:11Z",
      "updated_at": "2016-05-18T18:16:11Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "@terrajobst Ah! Thanks. I'm glad the arguments are safe on the server.\r\n\r\nWRT transparency: There is no indication at the time of install that the `dotnet cli` is automatically opted-into data sharing. There's no checkbox that will set the opt-out env var. There's no note or link to the GH issue or a Docs page that describes the program and how to opt-out. The privacy policy merely links to the generic MS privacy policy, where there is no mention of the program.\r\n\r\nYou really have to have heard about this through the GH issues or via chat at JabbR or Slack ... or Wireshark your server I guess. In my mind, that hardly constitutes \"transparency.\"\r\n\r\nIMO there is a great risk here for negative PR if the mainstream media gets a hold of this issue that will **not** be good.       "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Update on opt-out with `web.config`: My self-removal took a step forward with my custom `publish-iis` tooling, where I started shooting the env var into the `web.config` automatically.       "author": "Participant 27",
      "body": "I would like to point out, that, without informed, prior consent, collecting **any** personal information is illegal in most jurisdictions. There is sufficient precedent in the EU data protection directives 1995/46/EC, now superseded by [2016/679/EG](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32016R0679), as well as similar legislation in the state of New York (not sure which one at the moment) that collection of any data amounts to collection of personally identifiable information, as the time the data is collected and the information about where on the internet it is sent from can often, though sometimes inaccurately, identify a person, and is often treated as such information.\r\nThe only way you can comply with the legislation is to ensure every user of your software is prompted and asked for consent (which you cannot reliably do, as computers may be in shared use in a manner that should be obvious to you) or to make telemetry collection an opt-in setting as specified in pulls #7096 and #7098 .\r\nYes, I understand this means you will most likely not get any or poor telemetry results. You are going to have to live with that, or stop distributing your software in the aforementioned markets. Blocking telemetry requests on a geoIP basis on your servers does not meet the requirement.\r\nFeel free to contact the legal department. You may be liable for damages."

      "author": "Participant 41",
      "body": "Telemetry issue is becoming really very serious once you get with your project into any kind of protected data. Just receiving IP of machines on which CLI is running violates privacy rules as IP is regarded in most EU countries as personal data - it may allow identification of an individual. Obviously one may **turn it off after install** but since it is set to on during install by default it violates active opt in rules.\r\n\r\nDuring installation information on CLI telemetry is presented to users but it is not enough according to European Union regulations. If someone wants to collect any sort of data which is not related to basic functionality of provided software it is required by law to present to user active opt in choice with default setting during user interaction being opt-out. So no action from user always means \"no telemetry allowed\". \r\n\r\nMicrosoft entirely unnecessary exposes itself to legal risks at least in all EU jurisdictions ... fact that nothing happened in this area so far is no guarantee that it will not happen in future. Just learn from Facebook problems ...."
    },

      "created_at": "2017-10-10T12:16:57Z",
      "updated_at": "2017-10-10T12:16:57Z",
      "author": "Participant 42",
      "body": "Maybe what MS should do is build a telemetry manager that all of their tools plug into. Then users would have a central place to opt-in or out of telemetry collection for an entire systems.\r\n\r\nThe people complaining about this are probably the same people complaining about telemetry collection in every product that performs that function. If you centralize it, provide a way for people to inspect what is being sent back, and give it a big \"OFF\" switch, you could turn this whole story around. \r\n\r\nIt would probably also be a good idea to have a telemetry manager to control and protect the server end points that are taking data. Right now every team at MS is rolling their own system for collecting the data. Someone will end up getting that wrong and there will be a data breach. Formalizing your approach to collecting data on the \"client\" and sending to back end systems for reporting will protect MS as well as other entities. \r\n\r\nHow do you do that on Linux? That's really touchy. You could work with the distro vendors, and start an OSS project for the telemetry manager component. In the end, you are probably only going to be able to collect telemetry if you are VERY explicit about it during install on Linux systems. The overlap of privacy maximalists and Linux users is much higher than with Windows. \r\n\r\nIt's just going to keep coming up, and the \"we told you so\" moment is coming. You only have to get it wrong once. "

      "author": "Participant 24",
      "body": "My understanding, from reading the source, of what is happening\r\n\r\nThe runtime itself does not send telemetry so you shouldn't be sending any in telemetry production regardless of the environment setting by using the runtime package and running your pre-built app with the shared runtime by doing:\r\n\r\n`dotnet my.dll`\r\n\r\nThis is also confirmed as the [intention from the documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/telemetry)\r\n\r\n> Telemetry isn't enabled when using the dotnet command itself, with no command attached:\r\n> * dotnet\r\n> * dotnet [path-to-app]\r\n\r\nEqually a `self-contained deployment` will produce an executable file that requires nothing to be installed on the target machine and will not send any telemetry when running that executable.\r\n\r\nThe sdk *does* send telemetry; this is also confirmed as the [intention from the documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/telemetry)\r\n\r\n> Telemetry is enabled when using the .NET Core CLI commands, such as:\r\n> * dotnet build\r\n> * dotnet pack\r\n> * dotnet restore\r\n> * dotnet run\r\n\r\nThe first install/run at command line  that prints the message about `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` uses the `FirstTimeUseNoticeSentinel` which does ***not*** send any telemetry if it *also* is printing the message; so you are warned prior to it sending telemetry.\r\n\r\nIt does not send any telemetry after that if the `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` set to one of `true`, `1`, `yes` (case insensitive)\r\n\r\nThe HIPAA example @sushihangover gave compiles programs in production so it is using the full *sdk* rather than just the *runtime*.\r\n\r\nThe workarounds to the telemetry when using the sdk (`build`/`run` etc) as I understand them are:\r\n\r\n* either, set `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` environment variable\r\n* or, use `MsBuild` rather than `dotnet` to build your app - its what `dotnet` ends up calling and it doesn't send telemetry - its also less convenient; but what you'd probably be using on your build server\r\n\r\nNot sure what the Windows desktop installer does first time\r\n\r\n**tl;dr**\r\n\r\nIf you receive the message\r\n\r\n> Welcome to .NET Core!\r\n> `---------------------\r\n> Learn more about .NET Core: https://aka.ms/dotnet-docs\r\n> Use 'dotnet --help' to see available commands or visit: https://aka.ms/dotnet-cli-docs\r\n>\r\n> Telemetry\r\n> `---------\r\n> The .NET Core tools collect usage data in order to help us improve your experience. The data is anonymous and doesn't include command-line arguments. The data is collected by Microsoft and shared with the community. You can opt-out of telemetry by setting the DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT environment variable to '1' or 'true' using your favorite shell.\r\n>\r\n> Read more about .NET Core CLI Tools telemetry: https://aka.ms/dotnet-cli-telemetry\r\n\r\nThat use will not report any telemetry; but it will add a local sentinel file to mark that it has warned you\r\n\r\nRunning your app directly will not send any telemetry e.g.\r\n\r\n`dotnet [path-to-app]` rather than doing `dotnet run`\r\n\r\nThis is what you should be doing, generally, in production anyway, rather than using the sdk commands"
    },

      "updated_at": "2017-10-11T05:50:58Z",
      "author": "Participant 50",
      "body": "So, it is the case that after a year+ of this going on, that literally nothing of substantive has come from gathering this telemetry. I think it is time for it to go as it is just a leveraging point against dotnet, and does nothing to accomplish the real objective: wide-spread adoption of the CLI. In fact, it can be argued that it is now inhibiting this outcome.\r\n\r\nMaybe other CLIs do it, and maybe there is a vibe of irrationality with regards to the arguments waiving the banner of privacy (and we know Microsoft is not a big fan of privacy, if you want this opinion to change then demonstration by action is a great move), but no matter: It isn't actually accomplishing anything other than to distract people from real discussions about real possible features for the dotnet CLI. Or maybe that is the objective in itself: No such thing as bad press? That's just stupid PR if that's the case. Unless the objective is to lower your public perception so much so that no matter what step you take next there is only up; this is also a pretty distressing idea to consider.\r\n\r\nAnyways, if developers come to you with their opinions, you should be more than eager to oblige, and you should be operating from the perspective to adopt as many users as possible. Microsoft has not needed telemetry in the past to produce good products like Visual Studio (maybe I am wrong?) and so I struggle to see why you need it now. Good experiences are not built from telemetry, they are intuited by experienced designers or developed thoughtfully and iteratively. See the Tesla models, or the iPods, or even your very own Surface Book. \r\n\r\nI don't generally think that telemetry is harmful, but in this instance I do believe that it is harmful to the perception of the CLI. Additionally, there are people literally telling you: \"I wanted to use this, but I could not because of the telemetry feature\"; what a stupid reason to lose a customer over. There are many different avenues customers can be driven through to attract the same information that is being gathered here, normally opt-in related which is actually what you want in your telemetry anyways. Because, lets be honest: you don't actually care about the normal behavior, you want to hear about the joy points, and the pain points, and such responses are only elicited in the extrema. So long as you facilitate the reporting of bugs (does the CLI gather bug reports?), or opinion (does the CLI have opinion gathering mechanisms?) or so long as you peruse the internet/read GitHub, you are going to be OK.\r\n\r\nMaybe now is a good time to be reminded: You do not exist without your customers.  Spend a few cycles building things that will cultivate trust and open communication. Think outside the box for a bit, the \"me too\" behaviors are disheartening. \r\n\r\n\r\n"
    },

      "author": "Participant 23",
      "body": "@oaiey I think the JVM is clearly the future. You don't need the Oracle installer. It's mature, cross platform, has a wealth of mature libraries, tools and integrations and the build and deployment infrastructure is done and dusted.  You don't have to use Java if you don't want to either. It was the birth place of a lot of the design methodologies and bits of infrastructure that are crudely copied on the CLR.\r\n\r\nI'm really wishing I took the blue pill back in 2002 and went down the Java route at this point. The red pill was a bad choice.\r\n\r\nTo be clear, a lot of people are looking at HIPAA compliance as \"for use in medical devices\". This isn't the case. PII and control of data is the problem. Telemetry is fundamentally incompatible with that as it decreases the signal-to-noise ratio.\r\n\r\nAnother analogy: You don't design a secure system with the starting point of a sieve and try and fill all the holes with environment variables. You start with something that is locked down and open what you need. The problem is that telemetry uses the same protocols and ports as the legitimate and controlled data which adds noise and risk because every communication needs to be understood. That control has to happen in every part of the environment from the workstations the developers use, through to the build infrastructure, through to the production environment. And that is why Windows 10 and this sudden increase in telemetry in developer tooling is an absolute nightmare for us."

      "body": "I have read this thread again and I see there are a lot of concerns about Cloudflare, but there is nothing to say what to do instead.\r\n\r\nTo quote @BurungHantu1605 (https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/96#issuecomment-267805190) on Privacytools.io using Cloudflare: \r\n\r\n> The reason i decided to use CloudFlare was the fact that it's easy to setup, and nice to have a free ssl certificate. \r\n\r\nPersonally I am currently using Cloudflare for DNS hosting as I don't ever know when I might wish I had DDoS protection and I have past experience with both, the domain being unreachable during registrar transfer (and I think it's recommended to have registrar and DNS at separate places) and had a VPS terminated due to getting DDoSed. Later they have also introduced easy DNSSEC (https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/731).\r\n\r\nCurrently I am using GitHub pages directly with their LetsEncrypt certificate, but I am loading files from https://cloudflare-ipfs.com/ as that gives them global CDN and I don't know who else than I have the files pinned. I am using https://pinata.cloud/ but they are located in the USA (Five Eyes) and as I am European I think most of my visitors would also be European so I don't think it would make sense to use https://gateway.pinata.cloud/ .\r\n\r\n**TL;DR: What do you recommend me and everyone getting linked here to use instead?**"

      "body": "I received response by email linking to https://notabug.org/themusicgod1/cloudflare-tor and https://ieji.de/@crimeflare/101785817888174114 (thank you!).\r\n\r\n>> TL;DR: What do you recommend me and everyone getting linked here to use instead?\r\n>> https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/374#issuecomment-474987504\r\n\r\n> [1/2]\r\n\r\n> Personally I am currently using Cloudflare for DNS hosting\r\n\r\n> There are MANY alternatives.\r\n> https://dyn.com/dns/\r\n> https://dns.he.net/\r\n> https://freedns.afraid.org/\r\n> + Your hosting service/register's DNS service.\r\n\r\nWasn't Dyn.com evil or comparable to Cloudflare earlier? https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Dyn_cyberattack\r\n\r\nOn the other two alternatives you linked, I will need to investigate more.\r\n\r\n> Currently I am using GitHub pages directly\r\n\r\n> 1. Why don't you start building your server or buy VPS?\r\n> 2. Or https://www.reddit.com/r/webdev/comments/5m8tr4/how_do_i_host_the_website_i_just_built/dc1qpk7/\r\n> (Surge have free SSL service)\r\n\r\nServer building wouldn't help me due to being always behind CGN and flaky IPv6 (I have a Huawei 4G router and I think all of those seem to have a problem where they need to be rebooted often to not lose IPv6 connectivity) and it would cost money like a VPS and being unemployed I don't have money to put into it.\r\n\r\n> [2/2]\r\n\r\n> with their LetsEncrypt certificate,\r\n\r\n> Use Let's Encrypt or buy certificate.\r\n\r\n> I am loading files from https://cloudflare-ipfs.com/\r\n\r\n> It's censored. See https://ieji.de/@crimeflare/101779952797884218\r\n\r\nThe *\"Cloudflare IPFS experiment\" by Joe* (at [cloudflare-tor's PEOPLE.md](https://notabug.org/themusicgod1/cloudflare-tor/src/master/PEOPLE.md#blog)) seems to be a broken link as I am unable to access it with my local IPFS Go or IPFS.io gateway. Maybe Joe didn't have a device online enough often or no one has it pinned anymore?\r\n\r\nI have IPFS gateway as a variable anyway so I can change it with one line, but I think it's preferable for people to install [IPFS Companion](https://github.com/ipfs-shipyard/ipfs-companion/blob/master/README.md) to redirect traffic to their local gateway or wherever they prefer (by default https://ipfs.io/ipfs)\r\n\r\nPS. Can I also invite you to https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/785 on Mozilla's DNS over Cloud(flare) and what kind of advice should be given on it? Enforce something not-Cloudflare or disable it explicitly to miss out on encrypted SNI?"

      "author": "Participant 9",
      "body": "> I have read this thread again and I see there are a lot of concerns about Cloudflare, but there is nothing to say what to do instead.\r\n\r\nI've not tried to dig up dirt on Netlify, but that's one possible answer.  Netlify is gratis, will handle traffic to a github page, and comes with SSL.  I don't know the extent of their DDoS protection.\r\n\r\n> I received response by email linking to https://notabug.org/themusicgod1/cloudflare-tor and https://ieji.de/@crimeflare/101785817888174114 (thank you!).\r\n\r\nI'm very pleased to see that project is still going.  When it disappeared from github I was concerned that the project died.  Makes sense to move to notabug.org.\r\n\r\n> Wasn't Dyn.com evil or comparable to Cloudflare earlier? https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Dyn_cyberattack\r\n\r\nI've not heard that.  Your link just shows that Dyn.com was a victim.  It's also unclear from that article why those pissed at Equador for cutting Assange's internet connection would have a bone to pick with Dyn.com.  But I do see about 10 or so notoriously evil companies among Dyn.com's clientel.  Perhaps that's worth consideration.\r\n\r\n> it would cost money like a VPS and being unemployed I don't have money to put into it.\r\n\r\nCloudFlare is technically only gratis if you're not getting attacked.  When CloudFlare users get attacked, bandwidth goes up and CF considers that out of the scope of the gratis package and forces an upgrade to premium service.  So if your site is likely or expected to get attacked then CF is not really a gratis option anyway.  So if you need premium service, PerimeterX and Impurva Incapsula tend to be competitors of CF.  I don't know much about them, but no CDN exceeds the evil of CloudFlare.  So if CF is what you have you can do no worse AFAIK.  Netlify is worth a look first though.  They've been good for me but OTOH I've not been DDoSd."

    {

      "author": "Participant 12",
      "body": "Since my previous comment, I have migrated from Cloudflare to Gandi LiveDNS (my registrar). It's not entirely painless process, but here are the general steps:\r\n\r\n1. Disable DNSSEC at Cloudflare and Gandi if it was enabled. Cloudflare will say that they will disable it when the records are removed from Gandi who will recommend you to **not change your DNS servers for 72 hours!**\r\n    * I don't know if this is actually necessary, but I didn't find that much instructions on how to transfer DNS with DNSSEC enabled domain and decided that the safest route is disabling DNSSEC at the old provider and enabling it on the new one.\r\n2. Export your DNS zone in advanced DNS settings at Cloudflare.\r\n3. Import the zone to Gandi by editing some parts by hand (SOA and especially TTLs). Cloudflare will have TTLs set to 1 for domains with DDoS protection and Gandi's minimum is 300. This confused me, because Gandi only gave unclear error messages, but I have sent them feedback.\r\n4. Restore DNSSEC as Cloudflare isn't the only one providing one-click-DNSSEC anymore :purple_heart: \r\n\r\nIn case of IPFS, I changed my IPFS gateway variables from cloudflare-ipfs.com to ipns.co ([GitHub repo](https://github.com/VanVan/ipfsProxyHTTP))."

      "url": "https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/374#issuecomment-478322210",

      "updated_at": "2019-03-31T08:26:25Z",
      "author": "Participant 9",
      "body": "Subjecting visitors to CF is worse than subjecting them to bad performance.  So it was a good move.  \r\n\r\nI have some performance optimization suggestions:\r\n* [Specify](https://varvy.com/pagespeed/image-dimensions.html) the dimensions of all the images, so the important textual content can render before images are retrieved.\r\n* Link all the graphics to the sites they refer to offload the work of your server.  PTIO is promoting them, the least they can do is serve their own branded logos.\r\n* Any images that can't be linked to external sites could be isolated to a separate PTIO host.  If that host gets bogged down it doesn't matter because the important stuff is served by the server used for the landing page.\r\n\r\nBTW, I'm impressed with how viewable (and speedy) the page is in lynx.  Hopefully that never changes."

    {
      "id": 478342842,
      "url": "https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/374#issuecomment-478342842",

      "author": "Participant 13",
      "body": "Image dimensions is something I’ll work on today, I *think* we’re mostly good on that but there are definitely a few that need those specified. \r\n\r\nI don’t really think we should use third parties to host our images. We actually get a performance improvement from hosting them all ourselves with HTTP2, since there’s fewer external requests. Plus, for privacy related reasons I don’t think we should make all our visitors request third party resources where their servers may log traffic. With the current solution we can guarantee that there’s no access logging for web visitors. \r\n\r\nWhen I say we took a performance hit, it wasn’t that bad. Of course there was going to be a difference between a single server in Germany vs a network of hundreds of servers internationally serving our content, but we do have a high performance server and like you said, I think the trade-off was worth it to move off CloudFlare. \r\n\r\nI’m pretty happy with the results so far :)\r\n\r\nWe have our own Searx instance now, I’ll probably just link to that or a list of public instances once we get ours listed in more places. \r\n\r\nRegarding everything else, probably best if you open a separate issue for them, like PayPal. Not much I can do about that currently personally. "

      "body": "> We have our own Searx instance now, I’ll probably just link to that or a list of public instances once we get ours listed in more places.\r\n\r\nThere are a couple issues with that:\r\n* the PTIO instance is not filtering out CloudFlare results, making it less favorable for privacy than Danwin.\r\n* in light of the above, it will look like a biased or unjustified endorsement\r\n\r\nI would say if the PTIO instance filters out CF sites, then self-endorsement is well-earned and easily justifiable.  If not, then I think the best move is to list the Danwin searx instance which randomly selects a quality instance and then does the CF filtering on the results.  When the PTIO instance seems stable enough, the Danwin operator could be asked to ensure that ptio is among the selection.\r\n\r\nThere's nothing wrong with mentioning the PTIO searx instance, but it's a disservice to PTIO visitors to not make searxes.danwin1210.me the top recommendation."

  "title": "❌ Software Removal | github",
  "body": "# Drop Github, avoid Gitlab, endorse notabug.org\r\n\r\nSince PTIO was reorganized it's unclear if github is being endorsed.  There is no mention in the productivity category but the *participate* page links to github.  PTIO is leading by poor example in this case. Luckily it no longer appears on the front page.\r\n\r\nBefore continuing, it's worth mentioning that Github and Gitlab both distribute the free software that implements their service.  Unless I say otherwise, this post is about their *service*, not their software.\r\n\r\n## Privacy problems with Microsoft Github *service*\r\n\r\n1. MS feeds other privacy abusers:\r\n   1. Github uses Amazon AWS which triggers [several privacy and ethical problems](https://github.com/wireapp/wire/issues/265)\r\n   1. (2012) MS spent $35 million on Facebook advertisements, making it the third highest financial supporter of a notorious privacy abuser that year.\r\n1. Github may have a policy that entails censoring bug reports (see [this post](https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/763#issuecomment-482189305) for the discussion)\r\n1. MS supported CISPA and CISA unwarranted information exchange bills, and CISA passed.\r\n   1. (2018) MS [paid](http://cal-access.sos.ca.gov/Campaign/Committees/Detail.aspx?id=1401518&view=late1&session=2017) $195k to [fight privacy in CA](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2018/04/facebook-donated-200000-to-kill-a-privacy-law-but-now-its-backtracking/)\r\n1. MS supplies Bing search service which gives high rankings to [privacy-abusing](https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/374#issuecomment-460077544) CloudFlare websites.\r\n1. MS supplies hotmail.com email service, which uses vigilante extremist org *Spamhaus* to force residential internet users to share all their e-mail metadata and payloads with a corporate third-party.\r\n1. MS drug tests its employees, thus intruding on their privacy outside the workplace.\r\n1. MS products (Office in particular) violate the GDPR\r\n1. To report an MS security bug, one must sign in and the [sign-in page](https://msrc.microsoft.com/create-report) is broken.  It's really bad for security to make defect reports difficult to submit.\r\n\r\n### Privacy-compromising consequence of using Github for the PTIO project:\r\n1. (conflict of interest) PTIO selects only contributors willing to make privacy compromises, and excludes those who will not use GH for privacy reasons.\r\n1. (conflict of interest) When contributors are evaluating whether a tool is privacy-respecting, they white list Microsoft and Amazon as a consequence of PTIO using Github, and then [use that](https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/779#issuecomment-473503845) as rationale to endorse an unworthy tool.\r\n1. (side-effect) Privacy advocates who use GH face demoralizing criticism for what some regard as hypocrisy.  PTIO contributors should not be subjected to that.\r\n\r\n## Rationale for staying with Github:\r\n1. The shake-up of making a move will lose contributors.\r\n1. *e-voting* was mentioned, but self-hosted GitLab probably supports this (the GL service does).\r\n\r\n## Problems with Gitlab *service*\r\n\r\nMany Github refugees fled to Gitlab when Microsoft acquired Github.  It's a [bad idea](https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/742#issuecomment-481424035).  Gitlab should be avoided.\r\n\r\n## Alternatives\r\n\r\n1. self-hosting (Gogs, Gitea, Gitlab, etc.)\r\n   1. (+) avoids the \"shake-up\" problem of shrinking the community each time the project moves (there is no risk that the privacy factors would later take a negative turn).\r\n   1. (+) PTIO could host other privacy-focused projects and become part of the support structure for them.  Centralizing privacy-focused projects would increase PTIO visibility and establish a place where developers with the same high-level goals could develop in a more united way.       "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "I understand git, no worries on that score  ;-)   But the key thing about github is not the 'git' portion but rather the 'hub' portion.  If at some point it makes sense to switch away from github to self-hosted gitlab-in-a-box run by the privacyToolsIO folks, that will some at an immediate cost in community-size.  \r\n\r\nAs Mikaela is pointing out I believe, if there is federated login that DTRT rather than only kinda-sorta-working, you eliminate a good chunk of the lossage, because only the URL changes:  instead of filing issues a github.com/privacyToolsIO using their github credentials, instead people could file issues at git.privacyTools.io/self_referential_repo using their **github** credentials, which makes for a smooth transition with minimal lossage.  \r\n\r\nAnd it also helps if people that already have gitlab.com credentials, can use *those* to login at the new self-hosted self_referential_repo and so on.  \r\n\r\n>  as well as PTIO's mission against mass surveillance\r\n\r\nDisagree, this is blowing things out of proportion -- you have filed your boycott-github request in the 'wrong' place -- SoftwareRemoval instead of WebsiteIssue (or more properly WebsiteMetaIssue slash GeneralDiscussionOfAllTheThings).  Github is not a \"recommended privacy tool\" on the site, in a section written for the everday enduser audience, it is just \"here is where you can contribute and participate\" kind of thing, written for people who want to give back by participating in the FL/OSS process directly.  I.e. *not* everyday folks. \r\n\r\nThe masses do not typically need to find a way to self-host a git repo.  Because that is a very weird thing to need to do.  The masses need versioning-wiki-engines perhaps, with CRM attached most like, but not raw git repos -- most of the masses are not programmers and sysadmins, and those that are, can use local git repos or employer-provider version-control systems.  With luck their employer has read the hypothetical privacyToolsIO4Biz pages which detail how to run a privacy-respecting corporation including single-sign-on / cloud storage / collaboration apps / etc.  But the *employer* or more usually the employer's sysadmin, are not \"the masses\" in any sense, though they are individuals and citizens. \r\n\r\nThe masses do not typically need to find a way to file an issue in any git repo, either, whether it be on github or on gitlab or on codeberg or on notabug or self-hosted.  Because that is a bit of a weird thing to do.  But also because there are usually half a dozen other venues, sometime over a dozen.  \r\n\r\n>  [the newly-created partially-transplanted community at the newly-relocated repo] will be allowed to grow to include privacy-aware PTIO contributors who (quite rightly) do not use Github\r\n\r\nIn some ways you are the counterpoint here, because you use github despite being privacy-aware... and really, *because* you are privacy-aware.  But there are other venues:  mastodon instance, matrix chatroom, self-hosted by privacy-respecting people.  Who are already cross-posting things brought up in those areas, here to github.  Mikaela just posted something from the matrixChatroom where somebody had suggested \"libre videogames\" listings.  JonahAragon posted something similar, which was from an email-conversation (which is Not An Official Way to contact the project-maintainers because it does not scale... so dear readership please do not use that mechanism... but it does function as a fallback option of last resort methinks).  \r\n\r\nThe main question is not, how many people will we attract if we selfhost a gitlab-instance that refuse to use github... the main question is, are there benefits to gitlabSelfhosting that are impossible to achieve on github + mastodonSelfhosted + matrixHomeserver + reddit + twitter + maybeFacebook + discourseSelfhosted + keybase + lastResortFallbackToEmail?  I think the number of people that refuse to use **any** of those existing options, but *would* suddenly start using gitlabSelfhosted, is going to be dwarfed by the number of people that would stop contributing during the repo-switcheroo-shuffle because of hassle and switching costs and increased friction.  \r\n\r\np.s.  There is a different but related problem, which is that somewhere between six and nine official-or-quasi-official contact methods exist.  \r\n\r\n<details><summary>bifurcation of the overall privacy-community considered harmful</summary><p>\r\n\r\nAnd they all seem to be \"equal priority\" ...this bifurcates the overall community into tiny subcommunity-groupings and is a problem because there is no 'one main place' where everybody gathers habitually, plus 'specialized niche places' where particular sorts of work are done.  \r\n\r\nGoing out on a limb here, I think the One Main Place is probably going to be the discourseSelfhosted because it is most conducive to long-running async discussions, complemented by a github-associated wiki (or maybe a selfhosted wiki.js which is arguably cooler) where the *results* of discussions are summarized and stored.  Github issue-tracker is sub-optimal for discussion-threads because every comment emails a repo-watcher.  \r\n\r\nI think the chatroom area is fine for \"quick questions\" but unsuited to long involved discussions that happen over the course of many days.  I don't see keybase and keybaseChat as viable for any major role, though there is nothing wrong with the people that are code-signing the privacyToolsIO-branded online-services offerings being listed therein.  Similarly I don't think email directly to individual privacyToolsIO project-maintainers is a good plan... \r\n\r\nthat said, I would definitely signup for a daily&weekly BCC'd tips email-newletter and news-digest-blast, rather than get twitter&facebook versions of those things.  As long as privacyToolsIO mailing-lists are one-way info-blasts rather than bidirectional-conversations, that will keep the community from bifurcating needlessly (discussions of blasts will happen in discourseSelfHosted or in chatroom or whatnot -- each blast can link to an open forum-area even).  And because they are just simple bcc-based blasts they can be end2end encrypted via tutanota and protonmail and any other encrypted-webmail-provider that privacyToolsIO wishes to mention in the listings.  \r\n\r\nI think that twitter + reddit + facebook should be places where education-blasts are sent out and new participants are recruited, but should generally be privacy-propaganda-mouthpieces rather than \"community\" areas.  We don't want people on twitter talking about privacy, we just want to alert them via twitter and then help them transition to mastodon, ditto for alerting fbook denizens about friendica/diaspora, ditto for alerting reddit-participants to the new discourseSelfhosted.  And once they are signed up for encrypted webmail blasts, and transitioned to more privacy-respecting alternatives, they won't need to keep their twit/fbook/reddit thing around unless they want it for some strange reason :-) \r\n\r\n</p></details> \r\n"
    },

      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> If at some point it makes sense to switch away from github to self-hosted gitlab-in-a-box run by the privacyToolsIO folks, that will some at an immediate cost in community-size.\r\n\r\nIt's short-sighted to only consider the short-term cost and neglect the long-term benefit of being able to attract contributors who value privacy and have a strong enough constitution to avoid MS Github.\r\n\r\n> Disagree, this is blowing things out of proportion -- you have filed your boycott-github request in the 'wrong' place\r\n\r\nBullshit.  The direct attack on a PTIO contributor (@unnaturalnamed) was an attack on the PTIO mission.  There are numerous privacy abuses outlined in the OP, all exposed in support of the mission, which you continually work against.  Most of your posts favor mass surveillance.  This is the mission statement:\r\n\r\n\"*You are being watched. Private and state-sponsored organizations are monitoring and recording your online activities. privacytools.io provides knowledge and tools to protect your privacy against global mass surveillance.*\"\r\n\r\nIt is your comment that is in the wrong place.\r\n\r\n## The \"we are excluded from our own mission\" line of reasoning\r\n> Github is not a \"recommended privacy tool\" on the site\r\n\r\nThis was already addressed in #868.  Leading by poor example is no way to educate users.  It's a recipe for disaster because it (rightly) also harms credibility.  If the experts cannot demonstrate making privacy-respecting choices it signals to others they will struggle even more with the same thing.  You seem to have no idea how easily laypeople are put off by security matters.  It's fragile, and you propose showing them that the experts can't handle it either.  It's a demoralizing approach.\r\n\r\n> The masses do not typically need to find a way to self-host a git repo.\r\n\r\nIt doesn't matter.  It's displayed on the website in a big box on the front page.  Every tool users see PTIO using or pimping is an implied endorsement of that tool whether you want it to be or not.  PTIO is not even saying \"do as we say not as we do\", leaving it for users to assume MS Github is socially responsible and privacy-respecting.  And it shows experts that PTIO staff is not committed to their own mission.\r\n\r\n> In some ways you are the counterpoint here, because you use github despite being privacy-aware\r\n\r\nYou've just supported paragraph 3 under \"Privacy-compromising consequence of using Github for the PTIO project\".\r\n\r\n> The main question is not, how many people will we attract if we selfhost a gitlab-instance that refuse to use github\r\n\r\nOf course it is.  You're asking the wrong questions.\r\n\r\n> the main question is, are there benefits to gitlabSelfhosting that are impossible to achieve on github + mastodonSelfhosted + matrixHomeserver + reddit + twitter + maybeFacebook + discourseSelfhosted + keybase + lastResortFallbackToEmail?\r\n\r\nNo it's not.  That's what you concern yourself with if you're actually looking for excuses to use tools that undermine the cause.  It's an attempt at trading integrity for misguided guesswork that users visiting the webpage and learning there that PTIO has a Facebook account will then reach other users, as opposed to finding PTIO within the FB walled-garden of mass surveillance.\r\n\r\nIt's also a betrayal when coupled with the statement \"*privacytools.io provides knowledge and tools to protect your privacy against global mass surveillance.*\"\r\n\r\n> I think the number of people that refuse to use any of those existing options, but would suddenly start using gitlabSelfhosted, is going to be dwarfed by the number of people that would stop contributing during the repo-switcheroo-shuffle because of hassle and switching costs and increased friction.\r\n\r\nIt's the wrong question first of all, because only the \"would suddenly start using gitlabSelfhosted\" portion is relevant.  And whether it's \"sudden\" is over-stressed.  It's also short-sighted to blow an initial decrease out of proportion when the overall direction is commitment to the cause in a way that avoids hypocrisy.\r\n\r\nCredibility matters.\r\n"
    },

      "id": 486810114,
      "url": "https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/843#issuecomment-486810114",
